items.stem: What is meant by pressure?
items.answer: The force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Pressure – the force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface.

items.stem: Pressure is calculated as:
items.answer: force ÷ area

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Pressure increases when the area increases for the same force.
Reason (R): Pressure is force per unit area.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false: pressure decreases; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A force of 1000 N acts on an area of 0.02 m². Calculate the pressure.
Sneha stands on the floor and exerts a pressure of 2000 Pa. The total area of contact of the feet is 0.04 m². What is Sneha's weight?
A brick of weight 30 N measures 0.3 m × 0.15 m × 0.1 m. Find the largest and smallest pressure it can exert on the ground, and say which face it rests on each time.
items.answer: Largest 2000 Pa on the 0.15 m × 0.1 m face; smallest 666.7 Pa on the 0.3 m × 0.15 m face.
items.markingKey: Smallest area 0.015 m² gives P = 30 ÷ 0.015 = 2000 Pa; largest area 0.045 m² gives 666.7 Pa. 1 mark each area, 1 mark each pressure, 1 mark faces.

items.stem:
Read: Saanvi, of weight 450 N, stands in soft snow in Gulmarg. The total area of the soles of the boots is 0.025 m², and the total area of a pair of skis is 0.4 m².
(i) Find the pressure on the snow with boots. (ii) Find the pressure with skis. (iii) In which case will Saanvi sink less, and why? (iv) Give one other example where a larger area is used to reduce pressure.
items.answer: (i) 18000 Pa. (ii) 1125 Pa. (iii) With skis: the same weight acts on a larger area, so pressure is less. (iv) Wide straps of school bags / broad tyres of tractors / camel's broad feet.

items.stem: Define pressure and give its SI unit. Explain why (a) porters place a round cloth on their heads, (b) liquid pressure increases with depth, and solve: a box of weight 600 N rests on a base of area 0.3 m²; find the pressure.
items.answer: Pressure = force per unit area, Pa (N/m²). (a) the cloth increases the area of contact and reduces pressure on the head. (b) deeper water has more water above it pushing down. Pressure = 600 ÷ 0.3 = 2000 Pa.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition and unit; 1 mark each (a), (b); 2 marks numerical.

items.stem: A brick of weight 48 N measures 0.3 m × 0.15 m × 0.1 m. Find the largest and smallest pressure it can exert on the ground, and say which face it rests on each time.
items.answer: Largest 3200 Pa on the 0.15 m × 0.1 m face; smallest 1067 Pa on the 0.3 m × 0.15 m face.
items.markingKey: Smallest area 0.015 m² gives P = 48 ÷ 0.015 = 3200 Pa; largest area 0.045 m² gives 1067 Pa. 1 mark each area, 1 mark each pressure, 1 mark faces.

items.stem: A force of 450 N acts on an area of 2 m². Calculate the pressure.
items.answer: 225 Pa

items.stem: Why do school bags have wide straps?
items.answer: Wide straps spread the weight over a larger area, so pressure on the shoulders is less
items.markingKey: (b) Wide straps spread the weight over a larger area, so pressure on the shoulders is less.
options: Wide straps spread the weight over a larger area, so pressure on the shoulders is less

items.stem: Define liquid pressure.
items.answer: The pressure exerted by a liquid on the walls and base of its container and on objects in it
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Liquid pressure – the pressure exerted by a liquid on the walls and base of its container and on objects in it.

items.stem: Why do we not feel the very large atmospheric pressure acting on our body?
items.answer: The pressure inside our body is nearly equal and balances the outside pressure.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Water spurts farthest from the lowest hole of a water bottle.
Reason (R): Liquid pressure increases with depth.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read: Pooja made three holes at different heights in a tall plastic bottle filled with water. Water came out of all three; the stream from the lowest hole travelled the farthest.
(i) What does this show about liquid pressure and depth? (ii) Why does water come out sideways? (iii) What happens to the streams as the water level falls? (iv) Give one real-life application.
items.answer: (i) Pressure increases with depth. (ii) Liquids exert pressure on the walls (in all directions). (iii) They become weaker and fall closer. (iv) Dam walls are thicker at the bottom.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Air pressure is greater at the top of a mountain than at sea level.
Reason (R): There is less air above us at higher altitude.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Predict and explain what happens if you suck all the air out of a thin plastic bottle with its cap shut except for your mouth.
items.answer: The bottle gets crushed inwards because pressure inside falls and the higher atmospheric pressure outside pushes its walls in.

items.stem: Water comes out with the greatest force from the hole that is:
items.answer: lowest in the bottle

items.stem: Define monsoon winds.
items.answer: Seasonal winds that blow from the oceans towards land in summer and bring rain to India
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Monsoon winds – seasonal winds that blow from the oceans towards land in summer and bring rain to India.

items.stem: Warm air rises because it is:
items.answer: lighter (less dense) than cool air

items.stem: Why is the land breeze blowing at night from land to sea?
items.answer: At night land cools faster than the sea; air over the sea is warmer and rises, so cooler air from land moves towards the sea.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: land cools faster. 1 mark: air moves to low pressure over sea.

items.stem: Where should an air conditioner and a room heater be placed in a room—high or low? Explain.
items.answer: AC high on the wall: cool air sinks and spreads; heater low near the floor: warm air rises and circulates.

items.stem: Why does smoke from a chimney rise straight up on a calm day but bend towards the land on a summer afternoon at a seaside town?
items.answer: Hot smoke rises because warm air is less dense; in the afternoon, a sea breeze blows from sea to land and pushes the smoke inland.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rising hot air. 1 mark: sea breeze.

items.stem: Fishermen in Kerala sail out in the early morning and return in the afternoon. How do land and sea breezes help them?
items.answer: Early morning the land breeze (land to sea) carries the boats out; in the afternoon the sea breeze (sea to land) brings them back.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: land breeze out. 1 mark: sea breeze back.

items.stem: During the day, a breeze blows from the sea to the land because:
items.answer: land heats faster, air over it rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in
items.markingKey: (c) land heats faster, air over it rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in.
options: air always moves from land to sea
land cools faster during the day
land heats faster, air over it rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in
the sea heats faster than land

items.stem: Exhaust fans are fitted near the ceiling of a kitchen because:
items.answer: hot air rises and goes out through them
items.markingKey: (c) hot air rises and goes out through them.
options: hot air rises and goes out through them

items.stem: Air moves from regions of:
items.answer: high pressure to low pressure
options: cold to hotter places only at night

items.stem: The south-west monsoon winds in India come from:
items.answer: the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea
items.markingKey: (c) the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea.
options: the Indian Ocean and the Arabian Sea

items.stem: Define a tornado.
items.answer: A dark funnel-shaped cloud of violently rotating winds reaching from the sky to the ground
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A tornado – a dark funnel-shaped cloud of violently rotating winds reaching from the sky to the ground.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Early warnings by IMD save lives during cyclones.
Reason (R): Warnings give people time to move to safe shelters.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: How does warm, moist air over the ocean lead to the formation of a cyclone?
items.answer: Warm moist air rises, creating low pressure; water vapour condenses releasing heat, which makes air rise faster; surrounding air rushes in and spirals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rising air/low pressure. 1 mark: condensation heat and spiralling.

items.stem: IMD warns of a thunderstorm in your town during school hours. List three things students playing in the ground should do.
items.answer: Go indoors quickly into a building; avoid standing under trees or near poles; stay away from metal fences and water; if caught outside, squat low with feet together.

items.stem: Explain why cyclones weaken quickly after they move over land.
items.answer: Over land they lose their supply of warm, moist air from the sea, which provided the heat energy; friction with land also slows the winds.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: loss of moisture/heat. 1 mark: friction.

items.stem:
Read: An IMD bulletin says: "A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a cyclonic storm. Wind speed 90–100 km/h, gusting to 110 km/h. Landfall expected near Puri in 36 hours. Fishermen advised not to venture into the sea."
(i) Where did the cyclone form and why there? (ii) What is meant by landfall? (iii) Why are fishermen warned? (iv) Name one danger other than strong wind.
items.answer: (i) Bay of Bengal—warm ocean water provides warm moist air. (ii) The cyclone's centre crossing the coastline. (iii) High waves and winds can capsize boats. (iv) Storm surge/flooding/heavy rain.

items.stem: Which agency issues cyclone warnings in India?
items.answer: India Meteorological Department (IMD)

items.stem: Define a cyclone.
items.answer: A very large storm system with strong winds spiralling around a low-pressure centre
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A cyclone – a very large storm system with strong winds spiralling around a low-pressure centre.

items.stem: Why are heavy trucks fitted with many wide tyres?
items.answer: Many wide tyres spread the weight over a larger area, reducing pressure so the road and tyres are not damaged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: larger area. 1 mark: less pressure.

items.stem: A force of 250 N acts on an area of 2 m². Calculate the pressure.
items.answer: 125 Pa

items.answer: Wind blowing from the sea towards the land during the day
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A sea breeze – wind blowing from the sea towards the land during the day.

items.stem: Satellite images show a cyclone 600 km from the coast, moving at 15 km/h. Estimate how many hours people have before it reaches the coast, and why this information is useful.
items.answer: 600 ÷ 15 = 40 hours; this allows time for evacuation and preparations.

items.stem: A force of 450 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure.
items.answer: 900 Pa

items.stem: Why do mountaineers sometimes get nose bleeding at high altitudes?
items.answer: Atmospheric pressure is low, so the higher blood pressure inside can burst thin blood vessels in the nose.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: low outside pressure. 1 mark: vessels burst.

items.stem: A force of 600 N acts on an area of 2 m². Calculate the pressure.
items.answer: 300 Pa

items.stem: Why can a person lie on a bed of hundreds of nails without getting hurt, but cannot stand on one nail?
items.answer: The weight is shared by many nails, so the total area is large and the pressure at each point is small; on one nail the whole weight acts on a tiny area, giving huge pressure.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: many nails, large area. 1 mark: small pressure. 1 mark: single nail.

items.stem: During a thunderstorm, it is safest to:
items.answer: stay indoors away from metal objects and water taps
items.markingKey: (c) stay indoors away from metal objects and water taps.

stay indoors away from metal objects and water taps

items.stem: Why do hot-air balloons rise?
items.answer: The air inside is heated, becomes less dense than the surrounding air and rises, carrying the balloon.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: heated air less dense. 1 mark: rises.

items.stem: Why do nails have pointed tips?
items.answer: The small area of the tip produces a large pressure for the same force, so the nail goes into wood easily.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: small area. 1 mark: large pressure.

What is meant by wind?
items.answer: Moving air, which flows from a region of high pressure to one of low pressure
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Wind – moving air, which flows from a region of high pressure to one of low pressure.

items.stem: Prepare a list of five things a family in coastal Odisha should do when IMD issues a cyclone warning, with a reason for each.
items.answer: Listen to radio/TV updates (know path and timing); store drinking water and dry food (supply may be cut); keep a torch, batteries and first-aid kit; secure loose objects (they become missiles); move to a cyclone shelter if told (storm surge).

items.stem: A force of 500 N acts on an area of 0.1 m². Calculate the pressure.
Why does ink sometimes leak from a fountain pen in an aeroplane?
items.answer: Air pressure outside drops at high altitude while the air inside the pen is at higher pressure, pushing ink out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: lower outside pressure. 1 mark: inside pushes ink.

items.stem: A force of 50 N acts on an area of 0.02 m². Calculate the pressure.
An elephant weighs about 40 times more than a woman wearing pencil heels, yet the heels can damage a wooden floor more easily. Explain.
items.answer: The heel tip has a very small area, so the pressure it exerts can be larger than that of an elephant's broad feet.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: small area of heel. 1 mark: pressure comparison.

items.stem: What is meant by atmospheric pressure?
items.answer: The pressure exerted by the air of the atmosphere on everything on the Earth
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Atmospheric pressure – the pressure exerted by the air of the atmosphere on everything on the Earth.

items.stem: A brick of weight 20 N measures 0.25 m × 0.12 m × 0.08 m. Find the largest and smallest pressure it can exert on the ground, and say which face it rests on each time.

items.stem: Uneven heating of the Earth causes winds. Explain with one example.
items.answer: Air over hotter regions expands and rises, creating low pressure; cooler, high-pressure air moves in. Example: winds blow from the poles towards the equator.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: uneven heating → pressure difference. 1 mark: example.
